name: StreamYard
description: StreamYard is a browser-based live streaming, recording, webinar, multistream distribution, production, and team collaboration platform. Hosts use it to create studios, manage destinations and participants, broadcast live or prerecorded content, and retain or share recordings.
agentUseSummary: StreamYard cannot yet be connected through Relay. StreamYard explicitly says it does not currently offer a public API, while its documented studio, broadcast, destination, recording, and sharing workflows require interactive account access and carry host-controlled content, participant, destination, and privacy obligations.

blocked.label: Connect StreamYard
blocked.description: StreamYard says it has no public API and publishes no self-service application, scope, token, revocation, workspace-binding, webhook, or third-party automation contract for Relay to implement.

blocked.label: Read private StreamYard data
blocked.description: Studios, broadcasts, recordings, local tracks, destinations, participants, comments, brand assets, team data, analytics, webinars, registrations, and private links remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Create broadcasts or recordings
blocked.description: Creating, scheduling, starting, ending, or deleting live streams, prerecorded streams, recordings, webinars, studios, and destinations is blocked.

blocked.label: Produce or distribute content
blocked.description: Uploading media, changing branding, managing participants, showing comments or banners, sending destination messages, multistreaming, embedding, sharing, downloading, and deleting recordings are blocked.

blocked.label: Administer StreamYard
blocked.description: Workspace, space, team, role, plan, billing, SSO, storage, destination, webinar, audience, and account administration are blocked.

blocked.label: Use private StreamYard interfaces
blocked.description: Password or verification-code capture, browser automation, session cookies, scraping, reverse engineering, private or undocumented APIs, arbitrary embed harvesting, and raw exports are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No StreamYard action is enabled before StreamYard provides a documented third-party API contract and the exact workspace, roles, broadcasts, destinations, participants, content, recordings, and privacy boundaries are approved.

runtimeSupport.description: No StreamYard tools are mounted before an official third-party API and a bounded customer broadcast contract are approved.

providerSetup.blocker: StreamYard explicitly states that it does not currently have a public API and does not publish a self-service third-party application, authentication, authorization, endpoint, event, rate-limit, revocation, or workspace-binding contract. Its public help center documents signed-in interactive workflows for creating studios, selecting destinations, broadcasting, recording, embedding, sharing, downloading, and administering teams. Those workflows are not authority to automate the browser or private interfaces. StreamYard's terms place control and responsibility for streams, participants, content, third-party integrations, notices, and consents on the host, while its privacy policy treats hosts as controllers for audiovisual content, chats, and messages.
providerSetup.nextAction: Product, live-production, content, distribution, event, privacy, legal, security, and customer owners must choose one bounded StreamYard outcome and obtain StreamYard's current written API, application, commercial, platform, and data-processing terms. Freeze application ownership, authentication and revocation, exact account, workspace and space IDs, roles, destinations, broadcast types and states, participant and guest data, media and content rights, comments, webinars and registrations, recordings and retention, publication approvals, audit, rollback, deletion, rate, and termination rules. Only then may Relay implement typed bounded wrappers and provider acceptance.

evidence.supports: StreamYard explicitly says it does not currently have a public API and that an entire StreamYard studio cannot be embedded directly on a website.
StreamYard documents live studio creation, destination selection, per-destination title and description, and prerecorded streaming as interactive signed-in product workflows.

StreamYard documents materially different Owner, Admin, Creator, and Cohost permissions over billing, teams, workspaces, broadcasts, recordings, destinations, brand assets, comments, and participants.

StreamYard's current terms make hosts responsible for stream configuration, third-party integrations, participants, content, activities, notices, and consents, and restrict reverse engineering and unauthorized access or reuse.
StreamYard's privacy policy says hosts control personal-data processing connected to audiovisual content, chats, and messages, requiring an explicit customer privacy boundary before automation.
